title: Empirically probing the delegation-rationality boundary from a decision-theoretic misalignment model

original_idea.body: Pure-Python simulation of the delegation decision rule from A Decision-Theoretic Approach for Managing Misalignment (arXiv:2512.15584); reproduce delegate/don't-delegate frontier plus misspecification regret curve. No ML.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Delegation-rationality under misalignment is governance-relevant but the simulation's chain to catastrophic risk skips steps.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Pure Python simulation, no ML; accessible to a motivated beginner.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: reproduce frontier + regret curve; implementing the decision rule is bounded.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Long-horizon governance question, zero lab access, independent-friendly.

novelty.reasoning: Recent theory; empirical/simulation check is a plausibly-open angle.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Theory exists; simulation validation may be open.
